claims.statement: The concept applies to FPT, GHEC and GHES. Profiles present chosen information, contribution activity, selected repositories or gists, status and achievements; these are presentation features rather than complete activity or trust evidence.

The shared visibility warning applies only to FPT or GHEC and says public profile details are visible to all GitHub users; disclosure may expose identity-related risks. Disclosure is the user's choice, not a mandatory organizational policy.
Profile pronouns are conditional on a feature defined for FPT and GHEC, not GHES. The concept's broad product availability does not grant every element to every product.
A profile README is an optional customizable top-of-profile section using GitHub Flavored Markdown; example biographical, contribution and community-help content is not a required template.

The private-profile section is FPT-only. Privacy hides activity from other users without a specified-user exception; the owner can still see their information. This does not establish private repository access controls or delete activity.

For FPT private profiles the hidden elements include achievements, activity overview/feed, contribution graph, follower/following counts, Follow/Sponsor buttons, organization memberships, stars/projects/packages/sponsoring tabs and pronouns.
For FPT private profiles the optional README, bio and profile picture remain publicly visible. Private-profile status must not be treated as universal nondisclosure.

For FPT private profiles activity does not appear in others' activity feeds, discussion leaderboards, site-wide search results or Trending. Linked customization and reference pages are pointers, not reviewed by this receipt.
